description_full: National Beverage Corp., through its subsidiaries, develops, produces, markets, and sells a portfolio of sparkling waters, juices, energy drinks, and carbonated soft drinks in the United States and Canada. The company's Power+ brand portfolio offers sparkling water products under the LaCroix brands; non-carbonated water under the Clear Fruit; energy drink and shots under the Rip It brand; juice and juice-based products under Everfresh, Everfresh Premier Varietals, and Mr. Pure brands; and carbonated soft drinks under Shasta and Faygo brands. It serves retailers, as well as various smaller up-and-down-the-street accounts through the take-home, convenience, and food-service distribution channels. The company was incorporated in 1985 and is headquartered in Fort Lauderdale, Florida. National Beverage Corp. is a subsidiary of IBS Partners, Ltd.

financial_summary: National Beverage Corp. is a mid-cap consumer defensive business with a $3.5B market cap on $1.2B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +0% over the past three years and +5% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 75% against a 8% cost of capital — a 67-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 37%.

The business throws off $156M in free cash flow — roughly 13 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.99× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 75% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.4× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
